title: Generative AI and agent terminology in plain English
objectives: Explain generative AI, predictive AI, and an Agentforce agent using current Salesforce Help names.
Separate Einstein Generative AI, Prompt Builder, the Einstein Trust Layer, and Agentforce without collapsing them into one product.
State that Einstein Copilot for Salesforce was renamed to Agentforce, and that agent topics are now called subagents.
Refuse invented edition or SKU gates; mark them Needs verification unless Help cites them.
diagnostic_question: A VP asks for 'Einstein Copilot' to write Opportunity emails, score which deals will close, and chat with customers on WhatsApp. Before reading, which of those is generative, which is predictive, and which needs an Agentforce agent on a channel?
definition: On Salesforce, generative AI drafts language and other content from prompts and grounded CRM data. An Agentforce agent is a goal-oriented, autonomous AI application that can converse, choose jobs, and complete a sequence of tasks using business data. Predictive AI uses machine-learning models on historical data to forecast outcomes. ([Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm); [Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm); [Predictive AI](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_ai_predictive.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers still hear 'Einstein Copilot' and 'bot' used as if they were current product names. Help renamed Einstein Copilot for Salesforce to Agentforce. Mixing a draft-email prompt, a close-probability score, and a 24/7 service agent produces the wrong license conversation, the wrong test plan, and the wrong risk review.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel front desk. Predictive AI is the occupancy forecast on the night manager's clipboard. Generative AI is the clerk drafting a guest email from a template. An Agentforce agent is a trained night concierge who can talk to the guest, look up the reservation, and complete a sequence of jobs within standing orders—not merely draft a paragraph. Einstein Trust Layer is the sealed pouch and cameras on the way to the printer, not the concierge itself.
deeper_explanation: Salesforce Help describes Agentforce as the agent-driven layer of the Salesforce Platform: tools to create and customize agents for sales, service, marketing, commerce, Slack, and more, so agents work beside employees and can serve customers around the clock. Required add-on licenses vary by agent type. ([Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm))

Help defines AI agents as goal-oriented, autonomous applications that perform tasks and business interactions: they can initiate and complete a sequence of tasks, handle natural language, and securely provide answers drawn from business data. Agentforce Service Agent (ASA) is a service-specialized agent type that can work messaging channels and transfer complex or sensitive conversations to live reps, similar in that handoff idea to Einstein Bots—but ASA is not 'a bot with a new label' in Help. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm))

Predictive AI, in Data 360 Help, uses models built with machine learning and historical data to predict business outcomes and recommend ways to improve those outcomes. That is a score or forecast, not a drafted email and not an autonomous conversation. ([Predictive AI](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_ai_predictive.htm))

Einstein Trust Layer is a separate trust architecture: Help documents prompt defense, system policies that help limit hallucinations, and prompt-injection detection on user prompts for Agentforce and embedded AI. Do not treat Trust Layer as the agent product. ([Content Safety and Security](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_content_safety_and_security.htm))

Name hygiene from Help: Einstein Copilot for Salesforce is now Agentforce; beginning April 2026, agent topics are called subagents with no functionality change; as of 14 October 2025 Data Cloud was rebranded to Data 360. This lesson uses the current names and mentions former names only as aliases. Exact SKU packaging remains Needs verification unless a cited Help edition table covers the org.

mental_model.analogy: A hotel front desk on a busy night: the occupancy forecast, the drafted welcome note, and the night concierge who can actually complete jobs are three different roles sharing one lobby.
useful_mapping: predictive AI → occupancy forecast from history
generative AI / prompt template → drafted guest note from a form
Agentforce agent → night concierge who converses and completes a sequence of jobs
Prompt Builder → the stationery shop that designs reusable note forms
Einstein Trust Layer → sealed pouch, cameras, and banned-phrase screening—not the concierge
subagent (formerly topic) → a station the concierge is allowed to work (late checkout vs lost keys)
channel → lobby desk vs room phone vs partner hotel app
where_it_breaks: A real concierge is a person with legal duties; an agent is software with licenses, grounding, and actions.
Trust Layer services are not uniform across every agent type; Help states data masking can be disabled for some agents.
Einstein Bots still exist in Help as a related but distinct product; ASA is not a rename of Einstein Bots.
The analogy does not encode Einstein Requests, Flex Credits, or edition add-ons.

teach_back_prompt: Without using the words Copilot or bot as if they were current Agentforce names, explain generative AI versus an Agentforce agent versus predictive AI to a sales VP, then name one Help rename you would correct in their slide.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory: generative vs predictive vs Agentforce agent, plus the Copilot rename.
Given email-draft, close-score, and WhatsApp-chat requests, assign each to a term.
Explain Trust Layer versus the agent product and where hallucination controls live.
Walk a stakeholder who still says 'Einstein Copilot topics in Data Cloud' to current Help names.
Two-minute interview: terminology plus one SKU item you would mark Needs verification.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Generative AI drafts. Predictive AI scores from history. An Agentforce agent converses and completes jobs. Einstein Copilot was renamed to Agentforce. Trust Layer is the safety path, not the agent.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with the outcome. If they need a probability, that is predictive AI in Help. If they need a reusable draft the human still owns, that is generative via Prompt Builder. If they need a conversation that can select jobs and act, that is an Agentforce agent, with ASA as the service example. I correct Copilot to Agentforce and topics to subagents. I put Trust Layer next to hallucination and prompt-injection controls, not as a fourth product to buy by nickname. SKUs stay Needs verification unless Help's edition table matches the org.

terminology.plain: Software that drafts new text or similar content from a prompt and context.
terminology.precise: On Salesforce, generative features use prompt templates and LLMs; Help places them under Agentforce and Einstein Generative AI, with Prompt Builder as the template workshop.
terminology.example: A sales-email prompt template drafts a follow-up the rep still reviews.
terminology.non_example: A validation rule blocking a blank Amount is not generative AI.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Predictive AI: a score from history, not a drafted paragraph.
terminology.boundary: Prompt template types and evaluation are AI-003; this lesson only names the idea.

terminology.plain: An AI worker on Salesforce that can talk and complete a sequence of jobs inside guardrails.
terminology.precise: Help: goal-oriented, autonomous AI applications that perform tasks and business interactions, handle natural language, and draw answers from business data.
terminology.example: Agentforce Service Agent answering a shipping question on Enhanced Chat, then escalating a refund fight to a human.
terminology.non_example: A scheduled Flow that stamps Status every night with no conversation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Einstein Bots: Help still treats bots as a related but distinct product ASA can resemble for channel handoff.
terminology.boundary: Subagents, actions, and channels are AI-002.

terminology.plain: A model that guesses a future outcome from past data.
terminology.precise: Help: models built with machine learning and historical data to predict business outcomes and recommend ways to improve them.
terminology.example: A likelihood that a LAB_ renewal will churn, written to a score field.
terminology.non_example: An LLM drafting a churn-save email.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Generative AI: language, not a numeric forecast.
terminology.boundary: Which scoring product (Prediction Builder vs others) is Needs verification per Help for that product; AI-007 chooses among tools.

terminology.plain: Salesforce's safety path around generative AI: masking, audit, toxicity, prompt defense.
terminology.precise: Help documents Trust Layer policies for harmful content, prompt-injection detection, and system policies that help limit hallucinations on Agentforce and embedded AI.
terminology.example: Prompt injection detection applied to a user utterance before the LLM runs.
terminology.non_example: A profile permission set is authorization, not Trust Layer.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Agentforce: the agent product family, not the trust architecture.
terminology.boundary: Permissions, exposure, and human approval are AI-005.

terminology.plain: The Setup workshop where you design reusable prompt templates.
terminology.precise: Help: AI agents and other generative features use prompt templates created, tested, and managed in Prompt Builder, with merge fields, flows, and Apex as inputs.
terminology.example: A Field Generation template filling LAB_ Case_Summary__c from Case fields.
terminology.non_example: Typing a one-off question into a public chatbot outside Salesforce.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Agentforce Builder: designs the agent; Prompt Builder designs templates the agent or UI may call.
terminology.boundary: Template types, inputs, outputs, evaluation are AI-003.

terminology.plain: The old name for the default Salesforce employee agent type.
terminology.precise: Help release note: Einstein Copilot for Salesforce is now Agentforce, with no functionality change; Setup may show Agentforce or Agentforce (Default).
terminology.example: A stakeholder slide that still says Copilot should be corrected to Agentforce in an interview.
terminology.non_example: Using Copilot as if it were a separate current product beside Agentforce.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Microsoft Copilot: a different vendor's product.
terminology.boundary: Do not teach Copilot as the current Salesforce agent brand.

terminology.plain: One job the agent is allowed to do, with instructions and actions.
terminology.precise: Help: beginning April 2026, agent topics are called subagents; no functionality change. A subagent is a particular job an agent can do.
terminology.example: A Refund Request subagent with instructions and a create-case action.
terminology.non_example: A Chatter topic on a record feed.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Prompt template: the LLM instructions for one generation call, not the agent's job catalog.

terminology.plain: The model invents content that is not grounded in the allowed data.
terminology.precise: Help ties system policies to helping limit hallucinations and unintended LLM outputs; grounding and retrieval are the data side of the same risk.
terminology.example: An agent citing a return policy paragraph that is not in Knowledge.
terminology.non_example: A Flow formula that always returns 0.1 * Amount.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Wrong sharing: the model saw data the user should not see—that is exposure, AI-005.
terminology.boundary: Grounding details are AI-004; trust controls are AI-005.

When a design review still says agent topics or Data Cloud and you need the subagent and Data 360 aliases.

Do not use terminology flashcards to choose deterministic automation versus predictive versus generative versus an agent (AI-007).

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable Developer sandbox or scratch org; synthetic LAB_ records only. Skip enablement steps you are not licensed for.
starting_state_checks: You can open Salesforce Help in a browser.
You will not enable paid add-ons in production.
steps: Open Design and Implement Agents in Help and copy the Agentforce definition into LAB_notes.
Open Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent and write one sentence that distinguishes an agent from a prompt template.
Open Predictive AI Help and write one sentence that is not about drafting text.
List three former names (Copilot, topics, Data Cloud) and their current Help names.
guided_completion: If you cannot enable Agentforce, the lab is still complete: Help reading plus the written map.
If Setup still shows Copilot, record it as a transition leftover, not as the current brand.

decision_table.signal: Stakeholder wants a drafted email or field summary a human will send or save.
decision_table.choose: Call it generative AI and look to Prompt Builder (AI-003).
decision_table.not: An Agentforce agent as the default for every sentence of text.
decision_table.why: Help treats prompt templates as reusable generative drafts; agents are for jobs and conversations.

decision_table.signal: Stakeholder wants a probability or recommended next best numeric outcome from history.
decision_table.not: An LLM 'guess' with no model or historical training story.
decision_table.why: Predictive AI Help defines ML on historical data to predict outcomes.

decision_table.signal: Stakeholder wants 24/7 conversation that can complete a sequence of tasks and maybe escalate.
decision_table.choose: Call it an Agentforce agent; ASA is the service example in Help.
decision_table.not: Einstein Copilot as the current product name, or 'just Einstein Bots'.
decision_table.why: Help renamed Copilot to Agentforce and defines agents as autonomous task-completing applications.

decision_table.signal: Stakeholder asks how Salesforce stops prompt injection or invented policy text.
decision_table.choose: Name Einstein Trust Layer controls and grounding; defer depth to AI-004 and AI-005.
decision_table.not: A claim that the LLM 'cannot hallucinate' because it is Salesforce.
decision_table.why: Help documents prompt defense and policies that help limit hallucinations; it does not claim zero risk.

limitations: Does not configure subagents, actions, or channels.
Does not teach Prompt Builder template types in depth.
Does not choose Flow versus agent (AI-007).
Edition, add-on, and credit meters are Needs verification unless cited.
security_notes: Generative features can expose CRM data to an LLM path; Trust Layer is not optional vocabulary.
Never paste real customer PII into public LLM tools to 'demo Einstein'.
Do not claim data masking is on for every Agentforce type; Help says it can be disabled for some agents.
common_mistakes: Using Einstein Copilot as the current Salesforce agent name.
Calling every AI feature an agent.
Equating predictive scores with generative drafts.
Treating Einstein Bots and Agentforce Service Agent as the same product.
Stating edition gates that Help did not cite.

interview_questions.question: Explain generative AI, predictive AI, and an Agentforce agent in plain English.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Generative drafts content from prompts. Predictive scores an outcome from history. An Agentforce agent converses and can complete a sequence of jobs using CRM data. They are not one product.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep three buckets. Predictive AI in Help is machine learning on historical data to forecast outcomes—think a churn score. Generative AI is Prompt Builder templates that draft language a human or an agent may use. An agent is autonomous enough to select jobs and act, with ASA as the service example that can also escalate. I never call all three 'Einstein' and stop.

tradeoffs: Precision of language vs one-vendor slogan
Agent license cost vs a prompt template
weak_answer_warnings: Using Copilot as the current name

interview_questions.question: A hiring manager still says Einstein Copilot. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Help renamed Einstein Copilot for Salesforce to Agentforce with no functionality change. I use Agentforce, and I mention Agentforce (Default) if they mean the employee agent in Setup.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat Copilot as a former name, not a second product. I also mention the April 2026 topics-to-subagents rename so we do not fail a whiteboard that still says topics. If their org UI still shows Copilot, I call it a transition leftover and verify in Setup rather than arguing from a blog.
interview_questions.example: A slide titled 'Roll out Copilot topics in Data Cloud' becomes Agentforce subagents grounded with Data 360 / Agentforce Data Library.
tradeoffs: Correcting language vs shaming the interviewer
weak_answer_warnings: Inventing a third product called Copilot GPT

interview_questions.question: Sales wants AI to write emails, Service wants 24/7 chat, RevOps wants close probability. How do you split the work?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Emails are generative prompt templates. Chat that completes jobs is an Agentforce agent. Close probability is predictive AI. I will not stand up one agent to fake all three.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write three outcome sentences and three Help citations. Prompt Builder owns the sales-email template type. ASA or another agent type owns channels and escalation. Predictive AI owns the score field. Trust Layer is a cross-cutting control, not a fourth workstream with its own 'agent'. SKUs stay Needs verification until we read the edition table for that org.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ org: Sales Email template, Account churn score, ASA on Messaging for In-App and Web.
follow_ups: When do you refuse an agent?

interview_questions.question: Where does hallucination risk live in this terminology map?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: In the generative path: the LLM can invent. Help puts system policies that help limit hallucinations on the Trust Layer, and grounding on Data Library / RAG. It does not claim zero hallucination.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate invented facts from unauthorized facts. Invented facts are hallucination; unauthorized facts are data exposure and permissions (AI-005). Grounding (AI-004) reduces invented facts by retrieving allowed chunks. Prompt defense reduces injection. I will not promise the model cannot lie.
interview_questions.example: ASA cites a warranty clause that is not in LAB_ Knowledge—hallucination, not sharing.
tradeoffs: More grounding vs more human approval

interview_questions.question: Is Agentforce Service Agent just Einstein Bots?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. Help says ASA can transfer to live reps similar to Einstein Bots, but ASA is an AI agent type on Agentforce that uses Prompt Builder and Data Libraries.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I respect that channel and Omni-Channel patterns look familiar to bot admins. I then quote the agent definition: goal-oriented, autonomous, sequence of tasks, natural language, answers from business data. I do not tell a bot specialist their skills are useless; I tell them the reasoning layer is now subagents, instructions, and actions.
interview_questions.example: Existing Enhanced Chat that used a bot, now evaluated for ASA plus Omni-Channel flow routing.
tradeoffs: Reuse channel skills vs new reasoning model

interview_questions.question: What is Prompt Builder versus Agentforce Builder?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Prompt Builder authors reusable prompt templates. Agentforce Builder (and Agentforce Studio) is where you configure the agent. Templates can be used by agents and by other generative features.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help is explicit that agents and other generative features use prompt templates managed in Prompt Builder, including merge fields, flows, and Apex. The agent still needs subagents, actions, grounding, and a channel. I do not configure an agent inside a Field Generation template, and I do not write a 40-line prompt in Builder hoping it replaces an action.
interview_questions.example: Field Generation template on LAB_ Case versus ASA using Answer Questions with Knowledge.
weak_answer_warnings: Builder and Prompt Builder are the same Setup page

interview_questions.question: A solution architect lists Einstein GPT, Copilot, Agentforce, and Data Cloud as four current SKUs. How do you clean that up?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I map Copilot to Agentforce, Data Cloud to Data 360, and I refuse to treat Einstein GPT as a current Help headline without a cited article. I then split generative, predictive, and agent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open Help, not a 2023 keynote slide. I keep Einstein Generative AI as the Help section name that still exists, Einstein Trust Layer as architecture, and Agentforce as the agent product. Data 360 is the data platform name during and after the rebrand. Anything that sounds like a packaged SKU I mark Needs verification.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard rewrite in a design review with Help URLs in the corner.

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse to call a requirement an agent?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a formula, validation rule, or Flow already implements a deterministic rule, or when they only need a score or a single drafted field. Agents are for conversational, multi-step, guarded jobs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: AI-007 owns the full choice table, but this terminology lesson still needs judgment. Same-record math is not an agent. A nightly score is predictive. A one-click summary field is generative. An agent is justified when natural language plus a sequence of actions plus a channel is the actual requirement. I also refuse an agent when they cannot name grounding data or a human escalation path.
interview_questions.example: Request to 'AI-update Amount to Amount*1.1 on save'—that is Flow or a formula, not Agentforce.
